strips.title: The mind-door processes that follow a five-door process (tadanuvattika manodvāra-vīthi)
strips.src: the first consequent process: CMA IV guide; the series: later teachers (Ledi Sayadaw; Sayadaw Nandamālābhivaṃsa's Vīthi chart), NOT in the Saṅgaha
strips.note: the same visible form, just past

strips.title: Independent mind-door process, limited javana, clear object
strips.note: any object: past, present, future or timeless; for example, remembering the mango tomorrow

strips.title: Absorption process, first attainment of jhāna, slow faculties
strips.note: Absorption is the 5th javana. The four preceding javanas are one of the four great wholesome cittas with knowledge (great functional with knowledge, 47 48 51 52, for an arahant); joyful before jhānas 1–4, equanimous before the 5th jhāna and the immaterial. At the first attainment absorption occurs once; in a later attainment it can run for as long as resolved.

strips.title: Absorption process, keen faculties
strips.note: The preliminary moment is omitted, so absorption is the 4th javana.

strips.title: Path process (stream-entry), slow faculties
strips.src: CMA IV §14; IX (purification by knowledge and vision)
strips.note: Seven javanas: four preparatory, one path, two fruition. Change-of-lineage is the first citta to take Nibbāna as object, but it cannot cut defilements; the path does. Reviewing processes follow.

strips.title: Path process, keen faculties
strips.note: No preliminary moment, so three fruition moments follow the path: still seven javanas in all. (Round 1 had this reversed; corrected.)

strips.title: Attainment of cessation (nirodha-samāpatti)
strips.note: Only non-returners and arahants who have all eight attainments, and not in the immaterial planes: cessation needs the eight attainments in succession, and the fine-material jhānas cannot arise there (Vism XXIII). The preparatory moments are not shown.

strips.title: Death and rebirth (reference: Plate 10)
strips.note: Near death javanas run only five times, because the process is weak. Death can follow javana, registration or a life-continuum moment.
